newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht slides on dollar rally, stock weakness.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht slides on dollar rally, stock weakness.

text.p: The Thai baht fell sharply against a strong dollar in early Thursday trade and market concern about prolonged bearish Thai stocks, dealers said.
The baht fell to 25.970/25.980 to the dollar early from 25.927/25.933 late on Wednesday, dealers said.
"There were very active bids for dollar this morning. Sentiment on the baht was relatively weak following the stock market plunge yesterday," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
The Thai SET Index lost nearly three percent on Wednesday, partly on reports on an interest payment default by a major property company, brokers said.

"News on interest payment default by a property firm also triggered concern in the foreign exchange market about positions of commercial banks and finance companies," said another senior dealer at a local bank.
"Banks and finance companies have large loan exposure to the property sector," he said.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the baht/dollar mid-rate at 25.90, its lowest level since June 1990, and against 25.89 on Wednesday.
Dealers said some Singapore players also bought dollar to cover short positions on the eve of the Lunar New Year.
"Active dollar buying will likely ease in the afternoon after the Singapore market closes at noon," the dealer said.
